mainEntity.name: How many square feet is one pallet?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard GMA pallet is 48 by 40 inches, which is 13.3 sq ft of floor. That is the footprint, before any aisle space around it.

mainEntity.name: How do you calculate warehouse capacity?

acceptedAnswer.text: Take the usable floor, divide by the pallet footprint, multiply by stack height, then by cases per pallet. Here that is 1,650 sq ft, 124 spots, 248 positions, 12,400 cases.

mainEntity.name: How much of a warehouse is actually usable for storage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often around half to two thirds. At 55%, a 3,000 sq ft building leaves 1,650 sq ft of storage and 1,350 sq ft of aisles, dock, staging and office.

mainEntity.name: How much space does a food distributor need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Work back from weeks of cover rather than a square footage. 12,400 cases is 9.0 weeks at 6,000 a month, so the question is how many weeks your lead times force you to hold.

mainEntity.name: Is it cheaper to rack higher or to lease more space?

acceptedAnswer.text: Racking, nearly always. Going from 2 pallets high to 3 adds about 6,200 cases here, paid once, against rent every month for the same room.

mainEntity.name: What limits how high you can stack?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clear height, the reach of your truck, product weight and what the pallet below can carry. Check all four before you buy racking.

mainEntity.name: Why count cases instead of square feet?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because you buy in cases. A buyer cannot hold a purchase order against 1,650 sq ft, but they can hold it against a ceiling of 12,400 cases.
